approach: Root cause: the reading gate fixes criteria from the request text, and no step compares each criterion with the defaults that govern how criteria are judged (D43: a behavior criterion's evidence is commands the verifier ran, within its grant; D115; the append-only rule for docs/decisions.md and records/). Fix it at the gate with one new check, `check_judging_rules` (surveys.rs), registered as the last `step!` in `refusing_check` (checks.rs). It reads only the parsed criteria and deliverables and costs no model call. Round 3 narrows every matcher so that it refuses only a criterion that tells the job to do the forbidden thing, never one that describes code behavior or appends a new decision. (1) Decision-id edits: the edit verb must be in verb position (clause start, or directly after to/must/should/shall/will/and/then/please/also, or after 'by' for -ing) in its base form, and only determiner/entry words may sit between the verb and the id, so 'The fix is recorded as D174', 'docs/decisions.md is updated with a new decision D174' and 'This change adds decision D174' are accepted. (2) A `records/` path is refused in a criterion only when it is the direct object of an imperative edit verb, or the subject of 'is edited in place / by this change'; 'a commit that changes records/' and 'Fix the records/ loader' are accepted; the deliverable rule is unchanged. (3) Commands are read only from cited-run clauses (backticked spans right after run/running/execute/executing) and from an opening span only when ':' or a result verb follows it. The command rule is a table mirrored from this repository's athena.toml, tied to it by a drift test; D174 and the doc comment say it reflects this repository's grant, not a target's. (4) The git/host-write error says an Environment assumption does not let the verifier run it and points to a cited command the verifier can run. Wire in corpus cases, tests, a 13th reader-rule line, D174 appended at the end of the log (amends D43), a decision-links entry and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Read commands only from cited-run clauses. A cited span is a backticked span immediately after run/running/execute/executing (joined to further spans by ',', 'and', 'then', '&&', ';' or 'or'), or an opening backticked span only when what follows the closing backtick is ':' or one of the result verbs passes, passed, succeeds, succeeded, fails, exits, prints, shows, reports, returns, completes. Split each span into simple commands on `&&`, `||`, `;` and `|`. Spans elsewhere, and opening spans followed by anything else (for example '`cargo fmt --all` runs in the format step'), are unread. Answers finding 4.
decisions.reason: D43 judges the commands a behavior criterion cites as evidence (decisions.md:968-974), not commands the code under test runs. run/format.rs:1 says Athena runs `cargo fmt` on the work tree, and commits.rs:6 names `git merge --ff-only`; criteria about them must stay accepted, including when the span opens the sentence ('`cargo fmt --all` runs in the format step before `cargo fmt --all --check`' is an accept case). An opening span followed by ':' or a result verb is the shape 'X passes', which does cite X as evidence.

rejected.why: Refuses a code-behavior sentence that begins with a backticked command (critic finding 4).

decisions.choice: Judge a cited simple command against `VERIFIER_COMMANDS`, a constant table mirrored from athena.toml:76 and :108 (cargo: build, check, test, clippy, fmt, run, metadata, tree; git: status, diff, log, show; ls: *), plus `PRODUCER_ONLY_PROGRAMS` = rm, mv, chmod (producer_commands at athena.toml:74 minus verifier_commands). Refuse a cargo or git subcommand not in the table (cargo doc, install, publish; git commit, push), `cargo fmt` without `--check`, a leading `NAME=value` env prefix, a leading `env`, and a producer-only program. Do not read other programs (existing accept tests use `athena status`, `status`, `athena start`). Add test `judging_rules_table_matches_athena_toml` that does `athena_data::Config::parse(include_str!("../../../athena.toml"))` and, for every capability, asserts that verifier_commands equals the table and that producer programs minus verifier programs equal PRODUCER_ONLY_PROGRAMS. The doc comment and D174 say plainly that the table reflects THIS repository's grant, not the grant of a target's athena.toml, and that a target whose verifier grant is wider (for example allows `cargo doc`) would be refused wrongly until the live grant is passed in; D174 names that signature change as the follow-up. Answers finding 3.
decisions.reason: The rule D43 enforces is the verifier grant, which is data. The production caller does compute the live grant (`c.verifier_grant(jc).commands`, reading.rs:620-628) before it calls refusing_check (reading.rs:722), but refusing_check and check_reading_acceptance take five arguments (checks.rs:492-526) and are called from 14 sites in reading.rs plus checks.rs, replay.rs:55, run/mod.rs:2246 and :2316, and about 100 tests. Folding `repo_files` and a grant into a context struct touches every one of them, and the replay path has no grant at hand; it does not fit one producer run alongside the check itself. The table with a drift test gives a guard that fails in `cargo test` when this repository's grant changes. The target-grant gap is accepted, documented and named as the follow-up, which is why it is recorded as interim.

decisions.choice: Decision-id rule, applied to every criterion of any kind. Words are lowercased text split on white space, trimmed of leading and trailing characters other than letters, digits and '/', with trailing '.' removed and a trailing "'s" removed. Clauses are split on ';', ':', newline and '. '. An id token is 'd' plus 1 to 3 digits. A clause is read only if it has a decision-log word (`docs/decisions.md`, `decisions.md`, 'decision', 'decisions'). Verb position: the word is the first word of the clause, or is directly after one of to, must, should, shall, will, and, then, please, also (for -ing forms, directly after 'by'). Edit verbs, base form only: edit, rewrite, reword, revise, modify, update, correct, replace, remove, delete, overwrite, fix, change (-s, -ed forms are NOT triggers in rules i and ii). REFUSE when: (i) an edit verb in verb position is followed by an id with only these words between (at most 3): the, a, an, this, existing, old, current, entry, entries, text, wording, title, body, decision, decisions, of ('Edit D87', 'Rewrite the existing D87 entry', 'Update the text of D87'); (ii) append or add in verb position is followed within 4 words by to/onto/into/in directly before the id with no 'new' between ('append a note to D87'); (iii) the id is directly followed by is/are/gets/was and a participle edited, rewritten, reworded, revised, modified, overwritten, replaced, removed, deleted, changed, corrected, updated. SKIP an id that is the object of amend(s/ed/ing), supersede(s/d), cite(s/d), citing or 'refer(s) to' within 2 words before it; SKIP an id marked new: 'new', add*, append*, record*, creat*, introduc* within 4 words before it anywhere in the reading's criteria, or followed directly by 'is'/'was' plus recorded/added/appended/created ('The fix is recorded as D174'). A clause with no id is refused when it has `decisions.md`, 'in place' or 'existing entry/entries', and an edit verb in verb position. SKIP a verb when a negation (not, never, without, no, unchanged) is within 3 words before it, or one of the 3 words before it is criterion, criteria, reading, deliverable, text or rule. Answers finding 1. Worked through (all accepted): 'The fix is recorded as D174 in docs/decisions.md' ('fix' follows 'the', so it is not in verb position; D174 is marked new); 'docs/decisions.md is updated with a new decision D174' ('updated' is -ed; 'new' marks D174); 'This change adds decision D174' ('change' follows 'this'; 'adds' marks D174); 'Update docs/decisions.md to add D174' (the word 'docs/decisions.md' is not in the allowed between-set); 'CHANGELOG.md is updated to name D174' (no decision-log word); 'the fix changes the behavior D43 describes' (no decision-log word). Refused: 'Edit the existing D87 entry in docs/decisions.md in place', 'Rewrite D87 in docs/decisions.md to say X', 'Merge refusals no longer fire D87: append a note to D87 in docs/decisions.md', 'Edit existing entries of docs/decisions.md'.
decisions.reason: The gate never sees the log, so it cannot know that an id is new; the new-marker and verb-position tests make direct-object imperative edits the only trigger, and the plan's own accept list covers the nouns 'fix', 'change' and 'update' (critic finding 1). The cited 8gkv change is described by commit 620c657 'Stop pending-check merge refusals firing D87; append note to decisions' (HISTORY.txt:1095); rule (ii) refuses that wording without any word-based exemption. This job's own criterion 1 ('a criterion editing an existing D87 entry in place') is accepted: 'editing' is -ing without 'by', and 'criterion' sits within 3 words before it.

decisions.choice: `records/` rule in criteria, answering finding 2: refuse only a criterion that tells the job to edit it. (a) Imperative: an edit verb (edit, rewrite, reword, revise, modify, update, correct, replace, remove, delete, overwrite, fix, change, append, add) in verb position, followed by at most 2 words from {the, a, an, any, existing, old, file, files} and then a token starting `records/`, where either the token has a further path segment (`records/jobs/x/outcome.json`) or the next word is end of clause, in, to, so, directly, by, with, and, files, file, entries ('Correct records/jobs/x/outcome.json to say landed', 'Edit records/ files'). (b) Passive about this change: a `records/` token followed directly by is/are/be/gets and an edit participle, and then within 3 words 'in place' or 'by this change/job/commit/fix' or 'by the producer' or 'by hand' or 'manually'. The same negation and meta-subject skips apply. Not refused: 'A squash commit that changes records/ but names no job is refused by the records check' (changes is not in verb position), 'Fix the records/ loader in store.rs' (bare token followed by 'loader'), 'land updates records/jobs/<id>/outcome.json with the landed state' (updates is -s), 'records/ is not changed', 'counts read from records/'. Deliverables stay as before: any path under `records/` with any action, and Delete of docs/decisions.md, are refused; a Modify of docs/decisions.md is accepted.
decisions.reason: Athena's gate and store have records/ as their subject (crates/athena-gate/src/legacy.rs:61, athena.toml:163 'It changes records/ but names no job'). Criteria describing that behavior must stay accepted, as with commands in decision 2. The refused shape is the instruction to the job.

The error for a decision or records/ edit says to append a new decision to docs/decisions.md that amends the old one and never to edit records/. risks.risk: The matcher refuses a legitimate criterion, for example one that cites a command as part of the feature under test, one with a decision id near an edit noun, or one about the gate's or store's behavior toward records/.
risks.mitigation: Commands are read only from cited-run clauses and from opening spans followed by ':' or a result verb. Decision edits need a base-form edit verb in verb position, only entry words between it and the id, a decision-log word in the clause, and no new-id marker. records/ edits need an imperative or an 'in place / by this change' passive. The accept tests and 15 accept corpus cases cover each shape in the critic findings.

risks.risk: Known misses: a git write command or gh/curl written outside a cited span or with a program outside the table; a decision edit written without a decision-log word or in the passive without 'in place'; an edit with more words between verb and id than the allowed set; a negation, meta-subject or new-marker word used to dodge the check.
risks.mitigation: D174 and the doc comment name these limits. The check blocks the observed instances and their common phrasings; the verifier and D43's judge stay a second layer.

risks.risk: The command table drifts from the verifier grant, or the target's grant differs from this repository's (a target allowing `cargo doc` would be refused wrongly).
risks.mitigation: `judging_rules_table_matches_athena_toml` fails in `cargo test` when this repository's athena.toml changes. The doc comment and D174 state that the table is this repository's grant and name passing the live grant into the gate (a context struct beside repo_files, about 100 call sites) as the follow-up.

risks.mitigation: The command rule covers only what the grant states: the allowed subcommands and fmt with --check. It adds no rule the grant does not carry.
